items.title: Industry uses 'wrong' conditions for the Haber process
items.claim: The forward reaction N2 + 3H2 to 2NH3 is exothermic, and it reduces gas moles from 4 to 2. Le Chatelier says: high pressure, low temperature for maximum ammonia yield. Real plants run at 400 to 500 degrees Celsius — warm, not cold.
items.prompt: Why deliberately choose a temperature that lowers the equilibrium yield?

options.text: Cooling the reactor is impossible at industrial scale
The iron catalyst only works above 400 degrees
At room temperature the rate is so slow that even a high equilibrium yield is useless — moderate temperature is a compromise between rate (kinetics) and yield (thermodynamics)

items.reveal_title: Thermodynamics tells you what is possible; kinetics tells you whether it happens this century
items.reveal:
At 25 degrees Celsius the equilibrium for ammonia synthesis is excellent — but the activation energy is around 230 kJ per mol without a catalyst. The Maxwell-Boltzmann tail at room temperature has effectively zero molecules with that much energy. The reaction takes geological timescales.

The iron catalyst lowers the activation energy, and 450 degrees Celsius makes enough molecules energetic enough to react quickly. Yield drops to about 15 percent, but the unreacted gases are recycled. Throughput, not single-pass yield, is what matters.
items.why: Le Chatelier predicts the equilibrium destination. It says nothing about how fast you arrive.

items.title: The endpoint of a titration is NOT the equivalence point
items.claim: Titrate vinegar with sodium hydroxide using phenolphthalein. The colour changes when you've added enough base — that's the endpoint. Strictly, the equivalence point (exactly stoichiometric) and the endpoint (when the indicator changes) are two different things.
items.prompt: Why use phenolphthalein with weak-acid + strong-base titrations?

options.text: Its colour change at pH 8.2-10.0 matches the steep pH jump that occurs near the equivalence point in a weak-acid + strong-base titration; choosing the right indicator makes endpoint approximately equal to equivalence point

items.reveal:
A titration of ethanoic acid (pKa 4.76) with NaOH has equivalence point pH around 8.7 (not 7! — the conjugate base CH3COO- is itself basic). Phenolphthalein, with its colour change between pH 8.2 and 10, brackets this.

Methyl orange (pH 3.1-4.4) would change colour FAR before the equivalence point and give a wrong result for the acid concentration.

A strong acid + strong base titration has equivalence at pH 7 with a very steep pH jump — almost any indicator works. A weak acid + weak base titration has no sharp pH jump at all and is usually monitored with a pH meter, not an indicator.
items.why: Titrations are presented as if indicator change marks the answer exactly. The match between indicator pKa and equivalence pH determines accuracy.

items.title: Adding nitro to benzene changes WHERE the next reaction happens
items.claim: Nitrate benzene to make nitrobenzene. Try to nitrate nitrobenzene again. The first nitro group already attached doesn't just slow the next reaction — it controls WHICH carbon the new NO2 goes onto, even at carbons it doesn't touch.
items.prompt: Where does the second NO2 go?

options.text: Predominantly meta to the first nitro group, because NO2 is electron-withdrawing and destabilises the carbocation intermediates at the ortho and para positions specifically
Predominantly ortho/para, because the existing nitro stabilises adjacent positive charge
The reaction does not proceed at all

items.reveal:
Electrophilic aromatic substitution goes through a sigma-complex (carbocation) intermediate. Draw the resonance structures of that intermediate for ortho, meta and para attack. For ortho and para attack, one resonance structure puts the positive charge directly on the carbon bearing the existing substituent.

If that substituent is electron-donating (like OH or NH2), it stabilises that positive charge — so ortho/para wins. If it's electron-withdrawing (like NO2), it destabilises that positive charge — so ortho/para becomes UNfavourable, and meta is by default the least bad option.

This sub-ring-level energetics translates into hard rules students learn as 'meta directors versus ortho/para directors'.
items.why: Directing effects look like an arbitrary memorisation list. They are direct consequences of intermediate stability — derivable from first principles.
